title: What Happened Before the Stop: A Fixed-Size Black Box With a Hash Chain, Wrap-Around That Can Still Be Verified, and What Tampering Leaves Behind

questions.question: Why must recording to the black box never block, allocate or fail in the control loop?
options: A recorder that can stall the loop is a hazard of its own
questions.explanation: record is noexcept and the ring is allocated once.

questions.question: The ring has wrapped. A check that starts the chain at zero says what about the first event left?
options: Altered: it has lost its predecessor, so the box keeps the chain value of the last event overwritten and verify starts from it
questions.explanation: 12 dropped, from the kept link: yes.

questions.question: An event is deleted from the middle of the log. What does verify report?
options: gap: something is missing, and it is reported before the chain mismatch that the deletion also causes
questions.explanation: Swapped events are a gap at the first one out of place too.

questions.question: The last five events are cut off. What does verify say, and what would catch it?
options: It does not: the end of a chain has nothing after it to disagree, and it needs the latest chain value kept somewhere else

questions.question: The six events before the stop showed the range falling with the speed at 1.50 throughout. What does that tell you?
options: The robot did not slow for the wall at all, which the stop event with its cause bits alone would not have shown

questions.question: Why order events by sequence number and not by the clock?
options: The clock can be set back, and times 5, 4, 6 were kept in order by sequence and counted as one time going back
questions.explanation: The order is a fact of the box, not of the clock.
